macos-15.scope: All programs build one I64 array containing 0..N, hash the canonical tuple (iteration, array) with wrapping FNV-1a, and XOR the hashes. C/Rust encode the same schema directly; fwp uses ordinary pipes, generic type descriptors and immutable values. The iteration prefix changes each hash. One unprofiled RSS/warmup process precedes ten rotating wall/child-CPU samples including startup, input construction and printing; compilation and allocation profiles are separate. All use optimization level 2; C uses -ffp-contract=off. Buffered control restores only the old fwp ARC hash, not an older compiler. fwp counters distinguish managed storage from hash encoding-buffer requests/capacity; collection is disabled only for ownership profiles. C counts its explicit successful application malloc; Rust counts actual application allocator calls while its vector is live. These exclude allocator-internal and stdio storage; fwp managed counts can include output values. Peak RSS comes from uninstrumented programs. Ratios above one mean extra fwp time; no parity or universal speedup is assumed.
